scope: Royal residence at Sans-Souci, Milot, in its late royal configuration. Includes the main palace and its north double staircase, fountain and immediate rear approach.

references.filename: Le Palais Sans-Souci à Milot en Haïti, 1830.png

originalReview.notes: Clarke’s published north view shows the pavilion roofs, the tall center pediment and columned entry, paired stair arms, and side wing window rhythm of the royal residence. Palette, fine detail and the depth of the adjacent grounds are not recorded by the engraving.

publicDomainEvidence.sourceCitation: Charles Mackenzie, [[d:Q27463670|Notes on Haiti made during a residence in that republic]], H. Colburn and R. Bentley, 1830, Volume II.
[http://botanicus.org/page/1475767 Botanicus.com] (Carl Ritter: ''Naturhistorische Reise nach der westindischen Insel Hayti'', Stuttgart: Hallberger 1836.)

originalReview.notes: The 1836 plate after the 1820 visitor’s drawings independently supports the three raised pavilion roofs and two low roof links, front stairs, and the residence’s position above the parade ground. Neighbouring buildings are excluded from this model.

quallaSearch.notes: Searched Qualla first. Used Qualla’s exact 1830 engraving as the principal source. Its other cleared lithograph shows the parade ground with little usable palace detail. The creator-attributed 1836 palace plate corroborates the pre-earthquake roof and stair forms.
